discrepancies.claim: verbatim reads: 'No outright Nikkei row; Nikkei 225 follows the Equity line. Only Nikkei-labelled row (BTIC): "Nikkei/Topix BTIC | 00:00 | Globex Closed" (2019-new-years-holiday-schedule.xls).'
discrepancies.finding: The cited document — docs/2019-new-years-full-JAN2019.xls, sha256 6eafe7ee71c676299bd612eb3760d23d449c2111be8cee463d24308959e4d170, IA capture 2018-01-06T22:58:28Z, titled 'CME Group Globex New Years Holiday Schedule: December 31, 2018 - January 2, 2019' — contains no Nikkei row and no Topix row of any kind. Its complete list of Equity exception rows is: US Equity BTIC's & FTSE Emerging BTIC; FTSE Developed Euro BTIC; E-mini FTSE China 50 BTIC; E-mini FTSE BTIC; S&P CNX Nifty (Nifty 50). The companion compact sheet has no such row either. The quoted line is instead row [11] of a DIFFERENT year's document — zip2019/globex-trading-schedules/2019-2020-new-years-holiday-schedule.xls ('Nikkei/Topix BTIC | 00:00 | Globex Closed | ... | 00:00') — which this same JSON quotes correctly for 2020-01-01. The quotation was carried across years and attributed to a document that does not contain it.
discrepancies.impact: The row's status (closed) and open_instant (1700 CT / 2300 UTC) are independently correct from the DEC-2018 sheet's Equity Products line, so no holiday kind or instant is wrong. But a T1 quotation the evidence file would carry is not in its cited document, which is exactly the failure LAW-PRIMARY-SOURCES and the charter's 'quote verbatim / never infer from another year' rule forbid.
discrepancies.fix: Replace the quotation with what the DEC-2018 sheet actually prints (Equity Products line only) and state plainly that CME printed no Nikkei- or TOPIX-labelled row on that sheet.

discrepancies.where: 2021-12-23, five rows (equity_index, cryptocurrency, interest_rates, fx, energy), close_instant '1600 CT / 2200 UTC'
discrepancies.finding: The cited compact sheet prints 'Regular per Product' in the Thursday Dec 23 Close cell; the full sheet prints bare '16:00' under a header reading 'All times are Central Time   ET +1  UTC  +6'. The string '1600 CT / 2200 UTC' does appear on the compact sheet, but in the Monday Dec 27 column. So the UTC half is arithmetic from the header and the CT/UTC pair is borrowed from a different column. The JSON's own coverage narrative asserts 'no instant was converted or inferred'; that assertion is not true for these five rows.
discrepancies.impact: All five are status=normal, so no holiday row depends on them. The narrative claim should be softened.
discrepancies.fix: Record '16:00 (full sheet; sheet header: All times are Central Time, UTC +6)' and drop the unqualified 'no instant was converted' sentence.

confirmed_sound: Hash manifest: 86/86 entries re-hash correctly; every hashed file is present; no silent substitution.

Byte fidelity: 9 re-fetched documents (3 annual ZIPs, 5 per-holiday .xls across 2018/2020/2021/2022 captures, 1 archived index page) are byte-identical to the saved copies. All 65 ZIP members match the saved extractions.

Verbatim fidelity: 403 of 424 family rows' quoted fragments match the cited sheet exactly under whitespace normalisation; every one of the 21 exceptions resolves to a real cell or a disclosed annotation except D1.
Instants: 380 of 390 recorded CT/UTC tokens appear verbatim in the row's own cited document; the 10 exceptions are the formatting issue in D5, not wrong times.

No cross-year instant inference: every instant field traces to its own year's document. The task's per-year divergences were each verified against their own sheet — 2019-07-03 (Equity/Bitcoin 1215 CT early; Interest Rate/FX/Energy regular 1600 CT / 2100 UTC) vs 2020-07-02 (all five regular, only ags early); 2019-11-29 Energy 1245 vs Equity 1215; 2021-11-26 Cryptocurrency 1245 vs Equity/Rates/FX 1215 while 2019-11-29 Bitcoin was 1215; Good Friday 2019 and 2020 full closures vs 2021's partial session (Equity/Crypto 'Closed @ 0815 CT  / 1315 UTC', Interest Rate/FX 'Closed @ 1015 CT / 1515 UTC', Energy/Grains/Livestock/Lumber/Dairy 'Closed for Good Friday'); grains late-open on 2019-12-26 and 2020-01-02 but correctly NOT on 2021-01-04, where the sheet shows the normal Sunday 1900 CT open.

CME's own internal inconsistencies are preserved rather than silently corrected (e.g. Lumber 'Early @ 1205 CT/ 1800 UTC' on the 2019 Thanksgiving sheet, the '00;00' typo on the Presidents' Day sheets, 'ClOSE' column header on the 2020 July 4 sheet).

New Year's supplement: the DEC-2018 document's title is exactly as INDEX.md quotes it — 'CME Group Globex New Years Holiday Schedule: December 31, 2018 - January 2, 2019' — and it is genuinely the document that governs 1 Jan 2019, since each year's own 'new years' sheet runs 31 Dec into the following January.

'missing' list stands up to a fresh enumeration: a new CDX prefix crawl of cmegroup.com/tools-information/holiday-calendar/files/ (2018-2027, collapse=urlkey, 403 rows) contains no Juneteenth filename before 2022-juneteenth-advisory.pdf (capture 2022-01-28) and 2022-juneteenth-holiday-schedule.xls (capture 2022-06-20), exactly as claimed. Columbus Day and Veterans Day 2019-2021 appear only as *-advisory.pdf, *-otc-advisory.pdf and *-settlement-times.pdf. I read two of them (2021-columbus-day-advisory.pdf sha256 6288e5023a078a26..., 2019-veterans-day-advisory.pdf sha256 e69134f57c7bbb10...): both are 'IMPORTANT MEMORANDUM / FROM: CME Group Clearing' processing memos whose entire 'Trading:' entry is the line 'GLOBEX, Clearport and Trading Floor   http://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/holiday-calendar/' — no instants, no session language. Nothing the file lists as missing is in fact held by the archive.
Settlement-time and OTC-advisory PDFs are correctly excluded from keying any row (LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY).
Tier: all 424 rows are T1 and every one is a CME Group Globex holiday schedule read from the operator's own document.
bottom_line: The substance of cme-2019-2021 holds: all 44 dates and 424 family rows reproduce from bytes I re-downloaded myself, the statuses and instants are right, the per-year differences are genuinely sourced per year, and the 'missing' list survives a fresh enumeration. It fails verification on evidence discipline: one quotation (2019-01-01 Nikkei) does not exist in the document it cites and was carried over from another year's sheet; one manifested 'CME document' is a Wayback error page; and two of the three annual ZIPs have capture dates recorded as 2021/2022 when the archive's only captures are 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-30. D1-D3 must be fixed before these rows or their evidence file ship.
